---
title: "Assignment 6: NHANES EDA and AI Audit"
---

## Data and cohort definition

This analysis uses the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom CSV derived
from CDC/NCHS public-use NHANES files. The eligible cohort consists of
records with recorded age **20 through 80, inclusive**. Missing age and
ages outside this range are excluded. This restriction focuses the
exercise on adult BMI. No restriction by survey cycle is applied.

```{r}
#| label: load-and-define-cohort
# AI prompt: In R, load the NHANES CSV, keep adults aged 20–80, and print a knitr::kable() table showing the cohort counts at each step. Make the code work from either the repo root or three levels below it.
# Verified: Checked the actual CSV columns and boundary filter; rendered locally in a fresh R process.

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

csv_path <- "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
root_options <- c(".", "../../..")
repo_root <- root_options[file.exists(file.path(root_options, csv_path))][1]
if (is.na(repo_root)) stop("Cannot find the cached NHANES CSV.")

output_dir <- file.path(repo_root, "assignments/assignment06-eda-ai-audit/submission")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
nhanes <- read_csv(file.path(repo_root, csv_path), show_col_types = FALSE)
key_vars <- c("BMI", "Age", "IncomeGroup", "Gender", "Race", "Cycle")
stopifnot(all(key_vars %in% names(nhanes)))

adult_df <- nhanes |> filter(Age >= 20, Age <= 80)
stopifnot(nrow(adult_df) > 0, all(adult_df$Age >= 20 & adult_df$Age <= 80))

cohort_flow <- data.frame(
  Step = c("Prepared CSV", "Exclude missing age", "Restrict to ages 20-80"),
  N = c(nrow(nhanes), sum(!is.na(nhanes$Age)), nrow(adult_df))
)
kable(cohort_flow, caption = "Cohort definition before missing-data exclusions.")
```

## Missingness and analysis decisions

Missingness is assessed **before** excluding incomplete records. Percentages
use the age-eligible cohort as their denominator. BMI, age, and income
group are the Table 1 variables; gender, race, and cycle are additional
cohort checks. Missingness counts may overlap across variables.

```{r}
#| label: missingness
# AI prompt: Count missing values for six key variables before complete-case filtering.
# Verified: Matched missing counts to separate base-R counts; percentages use the age-eligible N.

missingness <- data.frame(
  Variable = key_vars,
  Cohort_N = nrow(adult_df),
  Missing_N = vapply(adult_df[key_vars], function(x) sum(is.na(x)), numeric(1))
)
missingness$Missing_percent <- round(100 * missingness$Missing_N / nrow(adult_df), 1)
kable(missingness, caption = "Missingness within the age-eligible cohort.")
```

Table 1 uses complete cases for **BMI, age, and income group only**.
Age is already complete after the age restriction. Records missing BMI
or income group are excluded; missing values in other columns do not
trigger exclusion. No missing values are imputed. This choice gives each
group's N, BMI, and age summaries the same denominator. Exclusion may
bias the results if retained and excluded records differ systematically.

```{r}
#| label: complete-case-flow
# AI prompt: Exclude missing Table 1 variables only and show the number removed.
# Verified: Checked complete-case N against base-R complete.cases on BMI, Age, and IncomeGroup.
table_df <- adult_df |> filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(Age), !is.na(IncomeGroup))
stopifnot(nrow(table_df) > 0)
kable(data.frame(
  Step = c("Age-eligible records", "Excluded: missing BMI or income", "Table 1 complete cases"),
  N = c(nrow(adult_df), nrow(adult_df) - nrow(table_df), nrow(table_df))
), caption = "Missing-data exclusions, counted once per record.")
```

## Table 1

N counts records retained in each income group. BMI (kg/m²) and age
(years) are presented as mean (sample SD), rounded to one decimal place,
following the classroom convention. SD describes variability among records.
These summaries do not display the full distributions or their tails.

```{r}
#| label: table1-and-export
# AI prompt: Summarize N and BMI/age mean (SD) by IncomeGroup and export the same table.
# Verified: Compared N, means, and sample SDs with independent base-R summaries; checked CSV read-back.
mean_sd <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(x), sd(x))
table1 <- table_df |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    `BMI, mean (SD)` = mean_sd(BMI),
    `Age, mean (SD)` = mean_sd(Age),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
stopifnot(sum(table1$N) == nrow(table_df))
write_csv(table1, file.path(output_dir, "table1.csv"))
kable(table1, caption = "Table 1. Complete cases aged 20-80; unweighted descriptive statistics.")
```

## Interpretation

The retained income groups have different observed mean BMI values in this
prepared dataset. These comparisons do not establish statistical
significance or show that income causes BMI differences. The exclusion
counts describe data availability; they do not establish that missingness
is random or that complete cases are representative.

## Methods and limitations

We analyzed the cached NHANES Health Equity classroom CSV using the
age-20-80 cohort defined above. After reporting missingness, we restricted
Table 1 to complete BMI, age, and income-group records and calculated
N and mean (SD) by IncomeGroup. This analysis is **descriptive, unweighted,
and non-causal**. Survey weights, strata, and primary sampling units were
not incorporated, and no hypothesis tests were performed. The summaries
describe retained classroom records; they are not national population
estimates. Complete-case selection, pooling cycles, and differences in
group composition limit interpretation. Population inference would require
an appropriate survey-design analysis and handling of pooled cycles.

## Provenance and stewardship

The data are cached in the course workspace for reproducible learning;
they were not retrieved afresh during this analysis. Only aggregate
summaries are reported. Row-level health records should not be pasted
into external AI tools, linked to identify participants, or used to make
individual-level or unsupported small-group claims.
